login.title: Sign in
login.purpose: Sign in or create a local account.
steps: Enter your email and password, or create an account (password of at least 10 characters).
questions: How do I create an account?
What does URBANOVA do?

projects.title: Projects
projects.purpose: Lists your projects and creates new ones.
steps: Give the project a name and set its location: click the map, search an address, or type latitude and longitude.
Optionally add a site boundary (GeoJSON polygon in WGS 84).
Tick the questions you want answered, then click Create project.
questions: What do I need to start a project?
Can I try it with sample data?

overview.title: 1 · Site
overview.purpose: The project dashboard: location, settings, the latest results summary, top hotspots and data completeness.
steps: Confirm the location.
Edit the project settings: objectives, AI text on or off, and the synthetic/test data flag.
Read the dashboard once an analysis has run.
questions: Why must I confirm the location?
What does the synthetic data flag do?

inputs.title: 2 · Inputs
inputs.purpose: Upload the design plan, planning documents, unit rates and optional data files, and review the imported plan features.
steps: Choose what you upload, pick the file and click Upload.
DXF files (and projected GeoJSON) need an EPSG code, e.g. 32636.
Review the imported features; confirm the units of a DXF without declared units.
Add unit rates for cost estimates (quoted prices only).
questions: Which file formats can I upload?
What is an EPSG code?
Why are my DXF features flagged?

rules.title: 3 · Planning rules
rules.purpose: Planning conditions found in your documents, which a person verifies before they are applied.
steps: Check each candidate rule against the quoted wording and page.
Verify or reject it; only verified rules are checked.
Resolve conflicting plot areas, and choose the site-area basis.
questions: Why isn't my rule applied?
Can it read Arabic documents?

readiness.title: 4 · Readiness
readiness.purpose: Shows which analyses can run with the current inputs and what is missing.
steps: Run the readiness check.
Fix what it lists as missing (boundary, plan, building heights, rules).
questions: Why is an analysis blocked?

scenarios.title: 5 · Scenarios
scenarios.purpose: The baseline design and up to 5 alternatives, including drafts made from recommendations.
steps: Create the baseline from the uploaded plan.
Create an alternative and edit it on the map or import features.
Approve drafts before they can be analysed.
questions: How do I make an alternative design?
What is a draft?

analysis.title: 6 · Run analysis
analysis.purpose: Starts analysis runs and shows their progress.
steps: Choose the analyses (keep Design hotspots selected).
Click Run all active scenarios so designs share the same settings and can be compared.
Wait: a run with live data takes a few minutes.
questions: How long does a run take?
Why did a module say unavailable?

results.title: 7 · Results
results.purpose: The map, metrics, findings, design hotspots and measured recommendations of one run, with AI insights and the results chat.
steps: Switch map layers and read the legend.
Open a hotspot card to see its causes and measured options with costs.
Ask detailed questions about the numbers in the results chat at the bottom of the page.
questions: What is a hotspot?
Why is a severity capped at moderate?
What do the AI labels mean?

compare.title: 8 · Compare
compare.purpose: Compares the baseline with alternatives analysed in the same joint run.
steps: Select the alternatives.
Optionally set criteria weights and a budget.
Read the trade-offs and what each design gives up.
questions: Why can't I compare these designs?
Why is there no single best design?

report.title: 9 · Report
report.purpose: Generates the PDF and HTML report and the data export of a run.
steps: Click Generate PDF + HTML report.
Download the report or the data export (GeoJSON and CSV).
questions: What is in the report?
Why is my report labelled partial or synthetic?
